connectivity_incident.symptom: both pods unreachable from the workstation 2026-08-11..2026-08-12 with 'could not open a kernel channel: [WinError 10060]', while git fetch succeeded throughout
connectivity_incident.ruled_out: ASGC and the pods themselves -- the owner's own JupyterLab tab worked and ran python3 -c 'print(1+1)' -> 2 in a pod terminal instantly
connectivity_incident.root_cause: every fresh TCP connection to the Taiwan host takes 21.2s, measured five times with no variance -- Windows' SYN-retransmit ladder (3+6+12s), i.e. the first two SYNs are dropped on the US->TW path and the third lands. requests hides this behind keep-alive; a kernel channel opens a fresh socket every time and always pays it.
connectivity_incident.why_the_timeout_parameter_did_not_help: websocket-client's own connect gives up at that ladder regardless of the timeout handed to it -- observed failing at 21.0s with timeout=30 AND with timeout=90, in the same script where a plain socket.create_connection to the same host:port succeeded at 21.2s
connectivity_incident.fix: Dicos._preconnect() establishes the socket where a 90s budget is honoured and hands it to websocket.create_connection(socket=...) already open; verified live immediately afterward
connectivity_incident.tls_guard: _preconnect() returns None for a non-http scheme deliberately: websocket-client skips its own TLS wrapping when handed a socket, so pre-connecting a wss:// channel would send plaintext to a TLS port
connectivity_incident.socket_leak_guard: the retry loop closes a socket it opened for a failed attempt, since the handover only happens on success
connectivity_incident.training_impact: none -- the trainer is a detached process on the pod and completed normally during the outage, confirmed from its own log rather than assumed

bug_fixed_this_session.symptom: bare subprocess.run(command, ...) with no timeout wrapping every call to scripts/dicos.py, used by both refresh() and (through it) watch_campaign_outputs.py's poll loop
bug_fixed_this_session.risk: dicos.py's own HTTP calls are individually bounded (30-300s), but nothing bounded the child process itself; a kernel-websocket exec that accepts a connection and never replies has no per-receive timeout on that path
bug_fixed_this_session.relation_to_open_incident: offered as a plausible mechanism for the still-unexplained 6h50m gap in the 2026-08-05 watcher run (15:18-22:17Z); not a confirmed root cause
bug_fixed_this_session.fix: 360s outer timeout (above dicos.py's largest internal single-request budget of 300s); subprocess.TimeoutExpired converted into the same SystemExit contract _dicos() already raised on nonzero exit, so latest_epoch()'s existing fallback and run_loop()'s existing catch-and-retry both cover it without further changes
bug_fixed_this_session.still_open: root cause inside dicos.py's kernel-websocket receive loop not found; a per-receive timeout there would close the gap properly instead of only bounding the blast radius

open_items.refresh_exit_code_wart: refresh() runs each per-family subprocess before prune_superseded_rows(), so on a fork transition that subprocess's trailing build_continuation_loss_figures.py step sees the un-pruned duplicate and raises. The post-prune block re-runs exactly those builders (by design, refresh_campaign_outputs.py:420), so the final state is correct -- but the failed subprocess's return code still poisons result['exit_code'], making a successful fork-transition refresh exit 1 with a traceback. The watcher is unaffected (run_once consumes the result dict, not an exit code).
